learning_outcomes.text: Students possess basic knowledge of physical quantities and physical relationships and can explain them.
Students can apply their specialized knowledge to practical problems.
Students identify physically relevant facts in complex problems.
Students derive mathematical equations to describe physical phenomena based on plausible assumptions and solve them.
Students record measurement data within the internship and evaluate it using common physical methods.
Students are able to independently familiarize themselves with new subject areas and successfully apply the acquired knowledge.
Students are able to evaluate the significance of measurement results.

syllabus_topics: Conservation laws (conservation of energy, conservation of momentum)
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written examination (grade). Successful participation in the internship is a prerequisite for taking the examination.
bibliography: Dobrinski, Krakau, Vogel: Physik für Ingenieure, Teubner Verlag
Hering, Martin, Stohrer: Physik für Ingenieure, VDI-Verlag
Kuchling: Taschenbuch der Physik, Fachbuchverlag Leipzig-Köln
